Summary: Someone new moved to Smallville, in the house on the other side of the Kent farm. Clark meets the new kid, Bruce Wayne, and his first impression isn't great. He thinks that Bruce is spoiled and rude and out of place. Maybe that's why he blows up at him. But he still saves him when he's in trouble, that's just the kind of person that Clark is. After a while they develop a tentative kind of friendship over the summer. Bruce isn't like anyone else that Clark knows, and he feels connected to him in all of his out of place-ness. Neither of them has worked out what ordinary looks like when you've spent three years earning it. This is the story about having the Thing. Bruce Wayne sits in a boardroom with the collar visible above his shirt collar and presents two billion dollars in contracts on four hours of patrol sleep and watches twelve people decide what to do with what they're seeing. Clark Kent sits across from his supervisor and is asked, for the first time in three years, whether he actually wants what he's been building — or whether it's the place he goes to not need anything. Ra's al Ghul comes back from the dead with an old claim. Lex Luthor sits in a courtroom. Gerald Gardener has been hoping since Bruce was eight years old. Dick Grayson has opinions.
